name: Akamu (pap) & akara

difficulty.label: Intermediate
drivers: Peeling the beans for akara is slow hand-work
Deep-frying at the right oil temperature takes a watchful eye
Whisking air into the batter is what makes akara light — easy to skip

time.overlap_note: Peel the beans ahead; the pap takes 2 minutes once the akara is frying.

substitutes: 4 tbsp custard powder as a faster swap

ingredients.prep: Soaked, skins rubbed off and rinsed clean.

steps.action: Rub the soaked beans between your palms to remove the skins, rinsing them away until the beans are clean.
steps.why: Skins make akara grainy and dark. Peeling is the effort that buys a smooth, golden fritter.
steps.watch_out: Float the skins off the top of the water.

steps.action: Blend the peeled beans with the onion, pepper and a little salt into a thick batter, then whisk it hard by hand for 2 minutes.
steps.cue: Batter is thick, pale and fluffy; a little dropped in water floats.
steps.why: Whisking traps air — that's what makes akara puff up light instead of dense.
steps.watch_out: Don't add much water; runny batter spreads and soaks oil.

steps.action: Heat oil in a deep pan. Test with a drop of batter — it should rise and sizzle. Scoop small balls in and fry until golden brown, turning.
steps.cue: Deep golden brown all over, ~2-3 min each side.
steps.why: Right-temperature oil seals the outside so they don't drink oil.
steps.watch_out: Too-hot oil burns the outside raw inside; too-cool oil makes them greasy. Medium-hot.

steps.action: For the pap: stir the akamu with a little cold water to a smooth, lump-free paste.
steps.why: Lumps won't dissolve once the hot water hits.

steps.action: Pour boiling water over the paste while stirring fast until it thickens to a smooth, glossy pap. Add milk and sugar to taste.
steps.cue: Thick, glossy, pours slowly off the spoon.
steps.why: Fast stirring with boiling water cooks and thickens it evenly.
steps.watch_out: Too thick? Add a splash more hot water.

doneness_signature: Light, golden akara balls beside a smooth, glossy bowl of hot pap.

rescue.problem: Akara soaking up oil / falling apart
rescue.fix: Batter is too wet or oil too cool. Whisk in a spoon of bean flour and raise the heat slightly.
Whisk hard, or pass it through a sieve.

level_up.how: Add finely diced onion and a pinch of crayfish to the batter.

name: Bread & egg sauce

difficulty.label: Easy
drivers: Only skill is not overcooking the eggs

steps.action: Heat the oil in a pan and stir the onion 1 minute until soft.
steps.why: Base flavour.

steps.action: Add the diced tomatoes and pepper, cook 3-4 minutes until softened and the rawness goes.
steps.cue: Tomatoes break into a loose sauce.
steps.why: Cooking out the raw tomato.

steps.action: Crack in the eggs, wait 30 seconds, then stir to scramble into the tomato mix. Season with salt and take off the heat while still soft.
steps.cue: Eggs just set, glossy and soft.
steps.why: Eggs keep cooking off the heat — stop early.
steps.watch_out: Overcooking makes them rubbery.

doneness_signature: Soft, glossy tomato-egg sauce to scoop with fresh bread.

rescue.fix: Stir a little fresh diced tomato through off the heat to loosen them.

level_up.how: Flake in sardine or corned beef and a pinch of crayfish for a fuller, richer sauce.

name: Fried plantain & egg

difficulty.label: Easy
drivers: Only watch the plantain doesn't burn

ingredients.prep: Peeled and sliced on the diagonal.
Beaten with a pinch of salt.

steps.action: Peel and slice the plantains diagonally and sprinkle with a little salt.
steps.why: Salt balances the sweetness.
steps.watch_out: Riper plantain = sweeter and softer.

steps.action: Heat oil and fry the plantain 2-3 minutes each side until golden. Drain.
steps.why: Caramelisation is the sweetness you want.
steps.watch_out: Medium heat — high heat burns the outside before the inside cooks.

steps.action: Pour the beaten egg (with onion/tomato if using) into the same pan on low heat. Let it set 1 minute, then fold or scramble.
steps.why: Low heat keeps the egg tender.
steps.watch_out: Don't dry it out.

doneness_signature: Sweet golden plantain beside soft, just-set eggs.

rescue.fix: Lower the heat and give each side more time.

level_up.how: Fold diced tomato, onion and pepper into the egg for a mini-frittata.

name: Custard & moi moi

difficulty.label: Easy
drivers: Assumes the moi moi is already made or bought

time.overlap_note: This assumes pre-made or store-bought moi moi. Making moi moi from scratch is a separate 90-minute recipe (see Moi moi).
make_ahead: Make or buy the moi moi

ingredients.prep: Pre-made or bought; warm it through.

steps.action: Mix the custard powder with a little cold water to a smooth paste with no lumps.
steps.why: Lumps won't dissolve once boiling water hits.

steps.action: Pour boiling water onto the paste while stirring quickly until it thickens, turns glossy and changes colour.
steps.why: Fast stirring cooks it evenly.
steps.watch_out: Too thick? Add a splash more hot water.

steps.action: Sweeten with sugar and milk, and serve with the warmed moi moi.
steps.why: A gentle, classic morning plate.

doneness_signature: Smooth glossy custard beside warm, savoury moi moi.

level_up.how: Use hot milk instead of water for the pour, and a pinch of nutmeg.

name: Boiled yam & egg sauce

time.overlap_note: Make the egg sauce while the yam boils.

ingredients.prep: Peeled and cut into medium slices.

steps.action: Boil the yam in salted water until a fork goes in easily, about 15-20 minutes.
steps.why: Tender but holding shape.
steps.watch_out: Don't overcook to mush.

steps.action: While it boils, heat oil and fry the onion 1 minute.
steps.why: Base.

steps.action: Add tomatoes and pepper, cook 3-4 minutes until soft.
steps.why: Cook out the raw tomato.

steps.action: Crack in the eggs, wait 30 seconds, scramble into the sauce, season with salt.
steps.why: Pull them slightly underdone.

doneness_signature: Tender yam under a soft tomato-egg sauce.

rescue.fix: Mash with oil and salt and serve as yam mash.

level_up.how: Add a pinch of crayfish and a little palm oil to the sauce.

name: Sweet potato & garden egg sauce
surprise_note: Most people boil or fry sweet potato plain. Pairing it with a quick garden egg sauce turns it into a proper savoury breakfast users rarely think to make.

difficulty.label: Simple
drivers: Garden egg sauce is unfamiliar to some but forgiving

time.overlap_note: Make the sauce while the sweet potato boils.

steps.action: Boil the sweet potato in salted water 12-15 minutes until soft. Drain.
steps.why: Soft but not collapsing.
steps.watch_out: Sweet potato cooks faster than yam — check early.

steps.action: Heat the palm oil and fry the onion 1 minute.
steps.why: Base.
steps.watch_out: Don't smoke the palm oil.

steps.action: Add the tomatoes, pepper and diced garden egg, cook 5 minutes until soft.
steps.cue: Garden egg soft and breaking down.
steps.why: Garden egg gives a mild, slightly bitter body to the sauce.

steps.action: Add crayfish and salt, and mash slightly so the sauce holds together.
steps.why: Mashing binds it.

doneness_signature: Soft sweet potato under a thick, savoury garden-egg sauce.

rescue.fix: Mash more garden egg in and simmer to thicken.

level_up.how: Add more palm oil and a little ground fish for a richer native sauce.

name: Indomie & egg

steps.action: Boil the noodles with the seasoning for 3 minutes, then drain most of the water.
steps.cue: Cooked but still with a little bite.
steps.why: Overcooked noodles go soft and break up.
steps.watch_out: Don't drown them — keep just a little sauce.

steps.action: In a separate pan, heat the oil and fry the onion and pepper 1 minute.
steps.why: Adds freshness beyond the seasoning packet.

steps.action: Pour in the beaten egg and scramble, then toss the drained noodles in and mix for 1 minute.
steps.why: Combining in the pan marries everything.

doneness_signature: Springy noodles tangled with soft scrambled egg and onion.

rescue.fix: Drain fully and stir-fry a minute to dry them out.

level_up.how: Add diced carrot, cabbage and leftover chicken or sausage.

name: Akara sandwich (akara & bread)
surprise_note: Akara is usually eaten with pap. Pressing it into bread as a sandwich is a street-style combo many home cooks never try.

difficulty.label: Intermediate
drivers: Whisking air into the batter for light akara

time.overlap_note: Peel the beans ahead to cut this in half.

steps.action: Rub the soaked beans between your palms to remove the skins and rinse them clean.
steps.why: Smooth akara needs peeled beans.
steps.watch_out: Float the skins off the top.

steps.action: Blend the beans with onion, pepper and salt into a thick batter and whisk hard 2 minutes until light.
steps.cue: Thick, fluffy; a drop floats in water.
steps.why: Trapped air = light akara.
steps.watch_out: Keep the batter thick.

steps.action: Fry small balls in hot oil 2-3 minutes each side until golden. Drain.
steps.why: Right oil temp seals them.
steps.watch_out: Medium-hot oil.

steps.action: Lightly butter the bread, press 2-3 warm akara balls in, close and gently flatten.
steps.why: Warm akara softens into the bread like a street sandwich.

doneness_signature: Soft bread pressed around crunchy-then-fluffy warm akara.

rescue.fix: Oil too cool — raise the heat and drain on paper.

level_up.how: Spread a little pepper sauce or ketchup and add sliced onion.

name: Golden morn / cereal & milk

steps.action: Pour the cereal into a bowl.
Add hot or cold milk/water to your preferred thickness. Sweeten and top with groundnut or banana.
steps.cue: Golden Morn thickens as it sits — add extra liquid.
steps.why: The no-cook option for rushed mornings.

doneness_signature: A quick, sweet, no-cook bowl with crunch on top.

rescue.fix: Stir in more milk or water.

level_up.how: Add groundnut, sliced banana and a spoon of powdered milk for a fuller bowl.

name: Nigerian pancakes

time.overlap_note: The batter rests 5 minutes while the pan heats.

steps.action: Mix the flour, eggs, blended tomato-onion, sugar, salt and enough water/milk into a smooth, pourable batter (thinner than cake batter).
steps.cue: Smooth and runs off the spoon in a thin stream.
steps.why: Thin batter makes thin, foldable Nigerian pancakes.
steps.watch_out: Whisk out lumps.

steps.action: Let the batter rest 5 minutes.
steps.why: Resting hydrates the flour for a smoother pancake.

steps.action: Heat a lightly oiled flat pan on medium, pour in a thin layer and swirl to spread.
steps.why: Thin and even cooks fast and folds neatly.
steps.watch_out: Too much oil makes it fry rather than set.

steps.action: Cook 1-2 minutes until the edges lift and the underside is golden, then flip and cook 1 minute more.
steps.why: Lifting edges mean it's ready to flip.
steps.watch_out: Flip with a wide turner so it doesn't tear.

doneness_signature: Thin, soft, savoury-sweet pancakes flecked with tomato and onion.

rescue.fix: Let the underside set fully before flipping; use a wide spatula.
Thin the batter with a little more milk or water.

level_up.how: Skip the pepper, add more sugar, milk and a pinch of nutmeg, and serve with honey.

name: Akamu & moi moi

difficulty.label: Easy
drivers: Assumes the moi moi is already made or bought

time.overlap_note: Assumes pre-made moi moi (see Moi moi for the 90-minute from-scratch version).
make_ahead: Make or buy the moi moi

steps.action: Mix the akamu with cold water to a smooth, lump-free paste.
steps.why: Lumps won't dissolve in hot water.

steps.action: Pour boiling water over it while stirring fast until thick and glossy. Sweeten with milk and sugar.
steps.why: Fast stirring cooks it evenly.
steps.watch_out: Adjust thickness with hot water.

steps.action: Warm the moi moi and serve together.
steps.why: Light, smooth and filling.

doneness_signature: Smooth glossy pap with warm savoury moi moi.

level_up.how: Make it with hot milk and a pinch of nutmeg.

name: Fried yam & pepper sauce

difficulty.label: Simple
drivers: Two parts: fry the yam, fry the sauce
Frying yam to golden without burning needs attention

time.overlap_note: Start the sauce while the yam fries.

ingredients.prep: Peeled and cut into chips or slices.

steps.action: Salt the yam slices, heat oil, and fry 3-4 minutes each side until golden. Drain.
steps.why: Golden crust, fluffy centre is the goal.
steps.watch_out: Medium heat — high heat burns before the inside cooks.

steps.action: In a separate pan, heat 2 tbsp oil and pour in the blended pepper-tomato.
steps.why: Start of the sauce.
steps.watch_out: It splatters.

steps.action: Fry the sauce 6-8 minutes until the rawness goes and oil floats on top. Add salt and stock cube.
steps.cue: Thick, oil floating, no raw smell.
steps.why: Frying out the raw pepper makes a smooth dipping sauce.
steps.watch_out: Stir so it doesn't catch.

doneness_signature: Golden fried yam with a thick, oily, fiery pepper dipping sauce.

rescue.fix: Lower heat and fry longer, or par-boil the slices 5 minutes before frying.

level_up.how: Flake sardine or corned beef into the pepper sauce.

name: Egg & veggie sandwich

difficulty.label: Easy
drivers: Only skill is not overcooking the egg

steps.action: Beat the eggs with the diced tomato, onion, pepper and a pinch of salt.
steps.cue: Veg evenly mixed through the egg.
steps.why: Mixing the veg in makes a filling that holds together in the bread.

steps.action: Heat a little butter or oil and pour in the egg. Let it set into a flat omelette, then fold to the size of your bread.
steps.cue: Egg just set, still soft, lightly golden underneath.
steps.why: A folded omelette sits neatly in a sandwich; soft egg keeps it moist.
steps.watch_out: Low-medium heat — don't brown it hard or it goes rubbery.

steps.action: Lightly butter the bread, lay the omelette in, close and press. Toast in the pan 1 minute a side if you like it crisp.
steps.cue: Golden, warm, holds together when cut.
steps.why: Toasting melts the butter in and crisps the outside.

doneness_signature: A warm, soft-centred egg sandwich, golden outside, veg flecked through.

rescue.fix: Add a thin smear of butter or a slice of tomato inside to bring back moisture.

level_up.how: Add flaked sardine or corned beef and a slice of cheese before you close it.

name: French toast (sweet)
surprise_note: Most people only think of bread for sandwiches — dipped in sweet egg and fried, the same loaf becomes a soft, golden treat.

difficulty.label: Easy
drivers: Only watch the heat so it doesn't burn before it cooks through

steps.action: Whisk the eggs with the milk, sugar and nutmeg in a wide bowl.
steps.why: Milk and sugar are what turn plain egg-bread into French toast.

steps.action: Dip each slice of bread in, letting it soak a few seconds each side.
steps.cue: Bread is soaked through but not falling apart.
steps.why: A proper soak gives the soft custardy middle.
steps.watch_out: Don't soak so long it turns to mush — a few seconds a side.

steps.action: Melt a little butter in a pan on medium and fry each slice until golden, about 2 minutes a side.
steps.cue: Deep golden, set in the middle, no wet batter.
steps.why: Medium heat cooks the custard centre before the outside burns.
steps.watch_out: Too hot and it browns before the inside sets — keep it medium.

doneness_signature: Golden, soft-centred sweet toast you can dust with sugar.

rescue.fix: Lower the heat and give it another minute a side to set.

level_up.how: Top with sliced banana, a handful of groundnut and a drizzle of honey.
